name: MI-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Democratic nominee McKinney won contested primary with solid fundraising and outside support
Republican nominee has no reported fundraising or outside spending
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~98%
model.rationale: The D+22 baseline and fundamentals point to a Safe Democratic hold, and the primary winner McKinney enters the general with a large financial edge over a Republican with no visible resources. Markets at 98% for Democrats confirm; I stay essentially at the baseline.
model.watch: A major outside-spending surge for the Republican nominee or a scandal involving McKinney could narrow the margin, though a flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Shri Thanedar (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Michigan's 13th District is a heavily Democratic Detroit-area seat with a D+22 partisan lean. Incumbent Shri Thanedar lost renomination, so this is an open seat, but the Democratic nominee, Donavan McKinney, is well positioned to hold it. He raised about $1.4 million and benefits from roughly $850,000 in outside support, far outpacing any opposition spending.

The Republican nominee, T.P. Nykoriak, has no reported fundraising, cash on hand, or outside spending, leaving little capacity to compete in a district this blue. Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability near 98 percent, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. The forecast stays close to the quantitative baseline of a roughly 24-point Democratic margin, with modest uncertainty given the absence of general-election polling.
